stem: A financial trading firm's Oracle database on Amazon RDS needs a guaranteed, consistent number of IOPS well above the baseline that General Purpose SSD storage provides, for its order-matching workload.

choices.text: Stay on General Purpose SSD (gp3) storage and enable RDS storage auto scaling on the volume
Move the workload to a burstable-performance (db.t) instance class to reduce cost
Add a read replica using General Purpose SSD storage to share the I/O load
Switch the storage to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) and provision the IOPS the workload needs

rationale: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) storage is built for I/O-intensive, latency-sensitive workloads and lets the team provision a specific, guaranteed IOPS rate above gp3's baseline, matching the order-matching workload's requirement. Growing a gp3 volume with storage auto scaling raises its baseline performance only up to gp3's own ceiling, not an arbitrary guaranteed rate above it. A burstable instance class can be throttled once its CPU credits run out under sustained load, working against a consistency requirement. A read replica shares read traffic; it does not give the primary itself a higher guaranteed IOPS rate.
